content: The term sheep dip refers to a liquid chemical solution containing insecticides and fungicides, which is used by shepherds and farmers to protect sheep from external parasites. These parasites include scab mites, blowflies, ticks, keds, and lice. The chemical solution is available in various forms, such as wettable powders, pastes, solutions, or suspensions, which are diluted or prepared for use. The term sheep dip can refer both to the chemical formulation itself and to the trough or container in which the sheep are immersed. The first sheep dip was created in 1830 by George Wilson of Coldstream, Scotland. This original formulation was based on arsenic powder and was exported via steamship from Berwick-upon-Tweed. Modern sheep dips are categorized into two main types: organophosphorus compounds and synthetic pyrethroids. Organophosphorus compounds, which were originally derived from chemical warfare agents, are highly toxic to humans and can be absorbed through the skin. Due to their hazardous nature, containers used to transport these chemicals over water must comply with United Nations regulations, which require that labeling remains legible even after immersion in water. However, sheep dips have been found to contaminate surrounding soil, leading to environmental concerns. In addition to its agricultural use, the term sheep dip has other meanings. In the business world, it is used colloquially to describe the process of providing general training to all employees on a broad topic. In the field of information security, sheep dip refers to an isolated computer system that is disconnected from the main business network. This system is used to screen incoming digital devices for malware and to monitor outgoing data packets for potential threats. In the context of the documentary The Men Who Killed Kennedy, the term is used to describe the deliberate dissemination of false personal information to create a cover story before engaging in covert intelligence activities. The term sheep dip has also been associated with illicit alcohol production. Some brands of bootleg whisky, such as Original Oldbury, were referred to as sheep dip by sellers to evade liquor taxes. This term is linked to the production and sale of moonshine. In popular culture, sheep dip has been referenced in various contexts. In the Monty Python Bruces sketch, a character named Bruce (played by Michael Palin) is humorously described as teaching logical positivism while also being responsible for the sheep dip. Additionally, Sheepdip is the name of a rock and roll band based in Rindge, New Hampshire. Lastly, Sheep Dip is the name of a brand of Scotch whisky.
